Commands use `shell: false`. Windows `.cmd` and `.bat` files therefore require an explicitly
authored command processor; direct invocation is a proven `SCRIPT_START_FAILED`, not an
automatic shell fallback. Resume and Replay keep the pinned command, arguments and
working-directory configuration. To change them, start a fresh run from the corrected definition;
neither Resume nor Replay applies the correction. The UI's **New run** uses a published version.
To test an unpublished saved draft, use `POST /loops/{id}/runs` with the editable draft's
`versionId` and `allowDraft: true`; the run freezes a new snapshot without publication.
Publishing can arm the new version's cron and webhook triggers and disable the earlier version's
registrations ([trigger arming](08-triggers-and-integrations.md#arming-decided-shipped-in-m6)). After an external prerequisite
repair, such as restoring a missing executable, ordinary Resume can retry the pinned definition. See
[Windows batch commands](guide/07-troubleshooting.md#windows-batch-commands) for an example.

changedParagraphs.text: Editing the loop does not change a failed run's pinned config. For a config or graph fix, start a fresh run from the corrected definition. The UI's **New run** uses a published version, so publish the correction before starting it there. To test an unpublished saved draft through the API, use `POST /loops/{id}/runs` with the editable draft's `versionId` and `allowDraft: true`; the run freezes a new snapshot without publication. Publishing can arm the new version's cron and webhook triggers and disable the earlier version's registrations; see [trigger arming](../08-triggers-and-integrations.md#arming-decided-shipped-in-m6). Resume and Replay retain the original pin. For a run ended by an exit with a failure outcome, inspect its result and start again as appropriate. An open inspector follows a resumed run live, whichever client resumed it; API snapshots, event pages and MCP show the same attempt.

`SCRIPT_START_FAILED` means the runner proved the command did not start. After restoring an external prerequisite, such as a missing executable, Resume can retry the pinned definition. If the command, arguments or working-directory configuration must change, start a fresh run from the corrected definition: use a published version for the UI's **New run**, or test the saved draft [through the API](#start-through-the-api) with the editable draft's `versionId` and `allowDraft: true`. Neither Resume nor Replay applies that definition change: both retain the failed run's pinned version. See [Windows batch commands](07-troubleshooting.md#windows-batch-commands). `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` means the previous attempt may already have produced its effect before its disposition was recorded. Recovery leaves it failed; **Recover script** opens an explicit choice: **Resume** runs it again in this run, **Replay** starts a new run from the failed node, **Cancel** leaves it failed. Both retry choices may repeat the effect. `failure.script` identifies the visit, dispatch, execution state and any known exit code. Completed nonzero exits still use `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE`.

Read `code`, `message`, `nodeId`, `resumable`, any `details`, and `inference` submission provenance when present. After fixing an external cause, resume when the failure is marked resumable. Start a fresh run from the corrected definition when the correction changes the pinned definition, using a published version in the UI or an explicit [API draft start](#start-through-the-api) with the editable draft's `versionId` and `allowDraft: true`. The contract lists every code below; some are reserved and current lower-level exceptions can appear as `INTERNAL_ERROR` instead.

For `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN`, the previous script attempt may already have produced its effect before its result was recorded. Recovery leaves it failed. Inspect the external system, then choose **Recover script**: **Resume** runs it again in the same run; **Replay** runs it in a new run from the failed node; **Cancel** leaves the run failed. Either retry may repeat the effect. `SCRIPT_START_FAILED` instead means the runner proved the command did not start. Restore an external prerequisite, such as a missing executable, then explicitly Resume. To change the command, arguments or working-directory configuration, start a fresh run from the corrected definition: use a published version for the UI's **New run**, or test the saved draft [through the API](03-run-and-observe.md#start-through-the-api) with the editable draft's `versionId` and `allowDraft: true`. Neither Resume nor Replay applies the change because both keep the pinned version. See [Windows batch commands](#windows-batch-commands). Nonzero completed exits retain `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE`. The failure's `script` fields identify the visit, dispatch, state and known exit code.

changedParagraphs.text:
To run a batch file, explicitly choose `C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe` (use your Windows
installation's actual path), set its arguments to `/d`, `/c` and the intended batch command,
and choose the working directory deliberately. `/d` disables the command processor's AutoRun
commands. The command string after `/c` is interpreted by that shell; keep it authored and
quote paths and arguments for `cmd.exe`, rather than inserting untrusted text. For example,
with a working directory containing `build.cmd`, the arguments are `["/d", "/c", "build.cmd"]`.
Start a fresh run from the corrected definition. The UI's **New run** uses a published version,
so publish the correction before starting it there. To test an unpublished saved draft, use
`POST /loops/{id}/runs` with the editable draft's `versionId` and `allowDraft: true`; the run
freezes a new snapshot without publication. Publishing can arm the new version's cron and
webhook triggers and disable the earlier version's registrations; see
[trigger arming](../08-triggers-and-integrations.md#arming-decided-shipped-in-m6).
Neither Resume nor Replay applies a definition change; both retain the old batch-file command.
If only an external prerequisite changed, such as
restoring a missing executable, Resume can use the existing pinned definition.

## Arming (Decided, shipped in M6)

The `TriggerService` in `apps/api/src/triggers/` owns everything between an external signal and `RunManager.startRun`.

- `POST /loops/{id}/publish` arms the new version: one `schedules` row per cron trigger node and one `webhook_endpoints` row per webhook trigger node. Rows of earlier versions of the loop are disabled, not deleted, so `GET /loops/{id}/triggers` shows the history. Runs in flight are unaffected (ADR-0008).
- Publishing is refused with 422 `LOOP_INVALID` (issue code `CRON_INVALID`) when a cron expression or timezone does not parse.
- Boot re-arms every loop's current version. Arming is idempotent per version: existing rows keep their next fire time, so a restart still sees what it missed, and a restored database without trigger rows gets them back.
- Deleting a loop disables its rows.
- `GET /loops/{id}/triggers` lists schedules, webhook endpoints (as `path: /hooks/<token>`, never the secret), and armed poll triggers.
